68ef1dfaaa.q: How did the 2026 autumn budget change Business Asset Disposal Relief limits for business owners?
68ef1dfaaa.a: The government has reduced the lifetime limit for business asset disposal relief from £1 million to £500,000 for qualifying disposals from the sixth of April next year, 2027. Not so long ago, it was at £10 million. The 18% capital gains tax remains unchanged, but for a higher rate taxpayer with at least £1 million of qualifying gains and no previous business asset disposal relief claims, the change would mean an additional £30,000 in capital gains tax, assuming the excess is taxed at 24%. HMRC estimates that approximately 13,000 individuals will be affected, while around 75% of claimants will remain unaffected.

68ef1dfaaa.rq: A business can become larger without actually becoming more valuable to a buyer, or equally, a business can become substantially more valuable without dramatically increasing the revenue growth.

b6b0dca9c6.q: What are the eligibility requirements for the new Founders Relief introduced in the 2026 autumn budget?
b6b0dca9c6.a: The new Founders Relief starting from April 6th, 2027 offers a 10% capital gains tax rate on up to £10 million of lifetime gains for qualifying founders and early investors. The eligibility requirements include significant ownership from the company's early trading period, a minimum five-year tax year holding period, substantial UK presence, at least £10 million turnover and 15 full-time equivalent employees, and qualifying combinations of rapid growth and research and development activity. HMRC estimates that only 600 individuals are going to qualify for this relief.

b7f4d409d1.q: What changes to employee share schemes were announced in the 2026 autumn budget regarding EMI and EOT structures?
b7f4d409d1.a: The budget announced an extension of EMI (Enterprise Management Incentives) eligibility for qualifying businesses preparing to transition to an employee trust, applying to relevant arrangements from April 6th, 2027. This shows government thinking that EMI schemes and EOT (Employee Ownership Trust) schemes could work together for benefit. However, the key insight is that giving employees a financial interest in the business doesn't automatically make them behave like owners; management capability and employee alignment need to be developed before choosing an ownership structure.

982d8b8063.q: Why should business owners focus on value creation over tax planning when planning an exit?
982d8b8063.a: A £30,000 tax difference is unlikely to justify selling a business prematurely. For example, an owner with a business worth £3 million—if better systems, stronger management, reduced owner dependence and more reliable earnings increase its value by just 10%—that's an additional £300,000 before tax and transaction costs. The potential improvement in business value is 10 times the maximum additional tax strategy. Tax planning and value creation need to be considered together; you shouldn't just react to tax changes that come along.
